questions.q: In Political Science and Civic Education, what is the best meaning of a **Federation**?
options: A political system where all administrative power is fiercely concentrated in one central capital city
A system of government where political powers and functions are constitutionally shared between a central government and its component states
A temporary alliance of countries designed solely for economic trading
A country entirely ruled by a traditional monarch
questions.explain: A **Federation** (or federal system) is a political arrangement where governing power is formally divided and shared by the constitution between a central authority (the Federal Government) and regional/state units.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: One of the fundamental needs for adopting a Federal system of government in Nigeria is to promote **Unity in Diversity**. What does this mean?
options: Bringing people of highly diverse ethnic, religious, and linguistic backgrounds together under one strong, united nation
Forcing every citizen to speak only one approved national language
Eliminating all regional differences by erasing historical borders completely
Creating independent sovereign countries for every single ethnic group
questions.explain: **Unity in Diversity** is the idea that although a country may contain hundreds of different ethnic groups and cultures (diversity), a federal system allows them to coexist peacefully as one politically united entity.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following is a core characteristic of a Federation?
options: The component states have absolutely no constitutional powers and can be abolished anytime by the President
Powers are shared, and the states have constitutionally defined control over their own internal affairs
The central government handles everything including minor rural street sweepers
There is strictly no written constitution guiding the government
questions.explain: In a federation, component units (states) are not just mere administrative agents of the center. They possess **constitutionally defined control and autonomy** over certain local affairs, shielding them from arbitrary federal erasure.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education

questions.q: Another crucial need for a Federation is **National Integration**. What role does federalism play in this process?
options: It strictly forbids citizens from traveling outside their state of origin
It fosters a sense of belonging among minority groups by giving them regional autonomy
It forces state governments to rely entirely on international loans
It empowers local thugs to act as state law enforcement
questions.explain: **National Integration** involves uniting disparate groups. Federalism assists this by ensuring power is decentralized, meaning minority groups have a level of political control in their regions, ensuring they feel integrated rather than marginalized.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In a Federation, what prevents the Central government from violently overtaking State governments and becoming a dictatorship?
options: The presence of international election observers
The Supreme and Rigid Constitution of the Federal Republic
The traditional chiefs who command independent tribal armies
The total absence of a federal police force
questions.explain: A defining characteristic of a federation is the supremacy of the **written and rigid constitution**. This constitution serves as the ultimate rule book that limits the powers of the central government, preventing it from overtaking state functions.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Federalism inherently involves power being shared among different levels. Which level is strategically designed to bring the government closest to the rural people?
options: The Federal Government
The State Government
The Local Government
The International Community
questions.explain: While Federalism officially dictates power-sharing between the Center and States, the creation of **Local Governments** acts as a third tier directly purposed to bring governance to the grassroots and rural populace.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Examine this equation representing the hierarchy of law in a Federation: Federal Law $+$ State Law $=$ Conflict. In a true federation like Nigeria, what is the standard constitutional resolution to this conflict?
options: The State law automatically overrides the Federal law
The Federal law prevails, and the State law is voided to the extent of its inconsistency
Both laws are immediately suspended until new elections are held
The State Governor dictates which law should apply in his state
questions.explain: In instances where a state makes a law that contradicts a valid federal law (especially on concurrent matters), the principle of the "Doctrine of Covering the Field" states that the **Federal law shall prevail**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The syllabus states that a major characteristic of federalism is that the "Central government controls the States" to an extent. Why is this supervisory relationship important?
options: To coordinate national economic policies and prevent any single state from engaging in activities that threaten national security or unity
To ensure state governors transfer all state revenue directly to the personal account of the President
To legally eradicate all minority ethnic languages in the country
To force all states to have the exact same physical size and population
questions.explain: While states are autonomous, the Federal (Central) government maintains certain controls (like national defense, emergency declarations, and foreign policy) to safeguard the **territorial integrity, economic stability, and national security** of the entire country.

questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Why must the relationships and powers of the three tiers of government be strictly written out in the Constitution, rather than left to verbal agreements?
options: To purposely confuse the citizens with complex legal terminology
To ensure they perform their functions according to legal provisions, thereby minimizing constitutional boundary clashes
Because written ink permanently guarantees immediate economic prosperity
So that traditional rulers can read them during annual festivals
questions.explain: A written constitution acts as an objective, binding contract. Detailing the powers ensures that each tier operates within its **legal limits**, which massively minimizes jurisdictional conflicts and power struggles.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A fundamental characteristic of a working Federation is that its Constitution must be **Rigid**. What does a rigid constitution imply in this context?
options: It is written on unbreakable stone tablets
It is entirely flexible and can be amended by the President single-handedly overnight
Its amendment process is strict, complex, and requires the joint approval of both the Federal legislature and a majority of the State legislatures
It cannot be read or interpreted by anyone except the Chief Justice
questions.explain: A **Rigid Constitution** requires a complex, highly demanding legal procedure to be amended. This is essential in a federation to prevent the central government from unilaterally altering the power-sharing formula to oppress the states.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A defining feature of the Nigerian Federation is the **Exclusive Legislative List**. What is the constitutional consequence if a State House of Assembly illegally passes a law concerning a matter perfectly situated on this Exclusive List (e.g., creating a state currency)?
options: The Federal Government must legally adopt the new state currency nationwide
The law becomes immediately unconstitutional, null, and void
The State House of Assembly is permanently exiled from the country
The matter is forcefully moved to the Concurrent list
questions.explain: Because the **Exclusive List** is reserved strictly for the Federal Government, any law made by a State Assembly concerning items on that list is completely invalid (**null and void**) as it breaches the supremacy of the constitution.
